summary: @arv-bedrock/auth preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated sibling payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it, chmods it executable, and then invokes the downloaded binary against a local file math_init.js (execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D,'math_init.js')])). math_init.js is a ~727KB '// @bun @bun-cjs' bundle using a rotated string-array obfuscator (WV8StW push/shift rotation over a large numeric/string table n7gIxM=[...]) so its real behavior is not visible to Node-based inspection. The package advertises itself as an auth library but ships stripped metadata (empty description, empty author, empty keywords, no repository) and no functionality consistent with that purpose — the only install-time effect is fetching a second-language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling script. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the payload is delivered under a runtime pulled in at install time so it evades Node-only static analysis, and it runs automatically on npm install via the preinstall lifecycle hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
